question: In 37 US airline accidents blamed partly on the crew, what failure turned up in most of them?
answer: A pilot not challenging the other's mistake. In 31 of the 37 accidents, reviewed by federal safety investigators, monitoring or challenging failed, most often a first officer not questioning the captain, who had usually made the first error. Two pilots are only safer than one if the second will speak.
move: A second pair of eyes is worth nothing without permission to speak.
ask: In my team, is there anyone who sees my mistakes but might not feel able to say so?
reference: National Transportation Safety Board, A Review of Flightcrew-Involved, Major Accidents of U.S. Air Carriers, 1978 Through 1990, Safety Study NTSB/SS-94/01, 1994
